payload.summary: supabase/schema.sql has not been replayable since before 2026-09-16; drift:manifest cannot run at all
payload.detail: Measured, not inferred. Replaying the pristine pre-branch supabase/schema.sql into the pinned supabase/postgres:17.6.1.127 container aborts with site_content_bootstrap_population_mismatch: the seeded bootstrap guard expects digest 57f6ec90225fc4341b446705f50a48b132f2872172d8f93888bf921fe7bfa1bc over 843 records, and the committed blob actually computes b3caf89c723fe87aa4602bc28f5aaeffb86d43dfcbdb938e93b0488ac7298b0a. Two independent methods agree on b3caf89c: a full container replay with the guard made self-reporting, and an offline reimplementation of site_content_canonical_json now committed in scripts/refresh-site-content-p03-baseline.ts. Consequences: npm run drift:manifest cannot be run on main, so supabase/drift-manifest.json can never be legitimately regenerated and tests/drift-detection.test.ts can only stay green while schema.sql never changes; and disaster recovery from schema.sql would fail. It is invisible because CI replays supabase/migrations via supabase migration up rather than schema.sql, and the offline drift test only compares schema_sha256. Repair is not local: site_content_retained_bootstrap_valid asserts r.id = site_content_release_id(r.release_digest, 0, 'bootstrap-v1'), so correcting the digest re-keys the bootstrap release UUID, which is hardcoded 36 times across the migration and schema.sql - including inside create function bodies already applied to the live database - and 12 more times in application code. That makes it an owner decision about the live clinical content control plane, in an approved window. A second guard, site_content_transition_backfill_unprovable, fires immediately after and needs the same re-keying to classify at epoch zero.
